vulnerabilities.description: HTML escaping functions exist but coverage is incomplete. Data attributes use escapeAttribute() properly, but task.text in js/view.js line 180 relies on Obsidian's MarkdownRenderer—if renderer changes, XSS risk emerges. Recommendation: Audit MarkdownRenderer.render() inputs.

hashString() implements FNV-1a but with reduced collision resistance due to truncation to 10 chars. While collision checks prevent duplicates in usedIds, malicious content could cause hash flooding. Impact: performance degradation, not code execution. Acceptable for non-cryptographic use.

Plugin data stored in plaintext (inlineKanbanHeadingFilters, taskKanbanTouchedAt). No encryption. Contains file paths and timestamps. Risk is low since data is local-only, but consider: user vault paths may reveal sensitive directory structures. Recommendation: Document data handling in manifest.

Raw HTML string (calloutActions) injected into markdown callout. Currently hardcoded, but if calloutActions ever includes user-controlled data without escaping, XSS risk. Recommendation: Sanitize any future dynamic content added to calloutActions.

RegEx TASK_LINE_RE and BLOCK_ID_RE are simple but no validation of extracted values before use. If vault contains malformed markdown, unpredictable parsing could occur. Low impact since validation happens at render time via escaping.

recommendations: Verify MarkdownRenderer.render() properly escapes task.text; audit Obsidian's rendering pipeline for edge cases with special characters.
Add explicit type validation for blockId format before use (whitelist alphanumeric + dash only).
Consider encrypting stored plugin data if vault paths or timestamps should remain private.
Document that calloutActions must remain static; add linter/test to prevent dynamic content injection.
Test escapeTableText() with Unicode, RTL text, and zero-width characters to confirm robustness.
Add Content Security Policy headers if this plugin ever loads external resources.
Audit file path handling in canEditInlineKanban() and findOpenMarkdownView() for path traversal (though Obsidian's API likely mitigates).
